body:
ASVS 4.0 - 1.14.2 verification requirement is:

`Verify that if deploying binaries to untrusted devices makes use of binary signatures, trusted connections, and verified endpoints.`

I would like to clarify from the community/maintainers of this project regarding the term `untrusted`. This control seems related to deploying server-side binaries (e.g. Jar files into Tomcat), right?  If that is the case, server is a trusted environment and not untrusted, making this control confusing. If not, then what does the term `untrusted devices` mean here? If our assumption is correct, then this control needs to either be reworded, else some examples would help about deployment of binaries on untrusted devices. 

Need to clarify what is meant by `untrusted` in this control. There was no clarification or heading explaining this subsection about "untrusted devices". Any information from the community would help regarding clearing up this ASVS verification requirement.

comments.body: - Make sure you are looking at the latest edits at: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/tree/master/4.0

@tghosth, woops my mistake as most of my opened issues come from the published ASVS 4.0 PDF. I should look at the latest edits as well before opening an issue. It seems the old ASVS 4.0 - 1.14.2 was already moved to 1.14.3 in the latest edits and it is now: `1.14.3 - Verify that binary signatures, trusted connections, and verified endpoints are used to deploy binaries to remote devices.` The problematic term `untrusted` for me was already addressed on the latest edit. 

Although, my understanding of this control is limited to deployment of server-side binaries (e.g. Jar files into Tomcat). Is my assumption correct? Or are there any other such binaries we are referring here (since this is ASVS for web and not mobile I would understand on mobile that this applies well, but not sure how much for web other than my example)?
Client server or desktop applications would be another example, no?

Isn't it that ASVS is for Web apps only, no? If we are including traditional old applications, then they could also fit this requirement as another example. Closing this issue since the control has been revised.
I think ASVS is intended to include desktop and client server apps as well. Mobile is different in principle because it has it's own different security model.

Respectfully, ASVS is for web and API apps only. Desktop threat model is 
so very different than web, it's much closer to the mobile threat model 
than a web app.

I politely suggest we both remote and "desktop app only" requirements 
and make it clear in the ASVS description that we're really the WASVS 
for the Web.

cc Daniel Cuthbert and Andrew V, am I right from your perspective?

Respectfully,

Jim Manico
